THE THREE INSEPARABLE PARTS:
1. ID CORRECTION at the real read sites: release-handoff-sources.ts (readFoundationArtifactForAttempt at :205, currently activation-keyed) and, if the watch horizon is restored, release-handoff-classify.ts's roster. Both must key on the id the writer writes.

The harness must seed EXACTLY deriveDispatchAggregateId(identity.attemptAggregateId) — seeding BOTH keys preserves the old tautology and makes a reader-regression mutant green.
3. ATOMICITY — THE DESIGN DECISION, and why this row is parked. foundation-artifact-ledger.ts:149-164 appends latest-wins (:231 reads latest after a re-seal), so a corrected id makes ARTIFACT a LIVE MUTABLE source. release-handoff-builder.ts:146-161 carries no artifact version into ReleaseHandoffBuilt.sources (:66-70 excluded it precisely because the old id had no writer), and attempt-release-fence-legs.ts:28-35 is capacity-bound: MAX_DECISION_LEGS=8, one primary + SEVEN fence slots exactly (ACTIVATION, BINDING, DISPATCH, JOURNAL, PROVIDER_RUN, RESOURCE, STEP at :52-54). An artifact can therefore move between the handoff's count capture and the release decision with every current fence passing — a stale-evidence authority hole. The two candidate designs: (a) widen MAX_DECISION_LEGS / redesign the leg schema to add an ARTIFACT fence (touches R3-8's delivered surface — coordinate with its owner and re-run its proof), or (b) make the artifact ledger immutable for a released attempt (single-seal or seal-freeze, a writer/ledger change with its own owner). NEITHER may be smuggled in as a side effect; the choice is the promotion gate for this row.

UNPARK CONDITION: a governor/human ruling in this row's comments choosing (a) or (b), with the owning surface named. Then plan all three parts together — partial landings re-open the hole task-fdcfe1ca closed.

STEP 3 — RED FIRST, WITH A CONSTRUCTIBLE DIVERGENCE. This replaces the impossible drill and is the heart of the re-plan.

WHY THE OLD ARM WAS IMPOSSIBLE, so it is not retried: the plan required a moved-`artifactDigest` case, but a lawful seal always yields `[]` — `artifactDigest` HAS NO PRODUCER, and foundation-attempt-store.ts:234 states the consequence outright: "artifactDigest has no producer. A REFUSED seal therefore never settles PROVEN." No input produces the divergence, so the arm and its D1 drill could never fail. Epic rail 7(A) forbids exactly that: a fixture that cannot distinguish the mechanism proves the system refuses, not that this guard refuses.

THE CONSTRUCTIBLE PROPERTY, under the ruled design (b): RE-SEAL IS AN ACTION A TEST CAN TAKE. Today foundation-artifact-ledger.ts:231 says "LATEST WINS: a re-seal after a further attempt event appends a second row" — so a second, DIFFERENT truth about one attempt's roster is currently reachable. Immutability is the refusal of exactly that for a release-bound attempt.
ARM A (REACHABILITY, DoD-2): a sealed artifact REACHES the handoff and CHANGES its output, through the production reader, with no fixture standing in for the writer. Assert the output difference, not merely that a read succeeded.
ARM B (IMMUTABILITY, DoD-4's (b) branch): seal an artifact, bind the attempt to a release, then attempt a re-seal with DIFFERENT bytes — the ledger REFUSES with its exact code AND layer, and NO second row appends. ARM C (IDEMPOTENCE PRESERVED): re-sealing with IDENTICAL bytes still replays cleanly and appends nothing. This is the arm that stops immutability being implemented as a blanket second-seal ban — the divergence between B and C is what proves the guard discriminates on the BODY, not on the attempt.
